text:
Related 2023–2026 research supports text–behavior alignment, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of a jointly trained, randomly initialized text encoder, removable auxiliary branch, and unchanged NextItNet inference. [ADRec (2025)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705125003375) aligns sequence and target-item text representations using supervised and self-supervised contrastive signals. [LLM2Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21579) emphasizes that textual semantics alone miss collaborative relationships and trains representations to incorporate interaction signals; its pretrained LLM makes the full method unsuitable here. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) identifies poor item differentiation from anisotropic pretrained text embeddings, motivating checks for representation collapse and excessive similarity, although its setting differs from scratch training.

A constraint-compatible hypothesis—not a demonstrated result from these papers—is to retain NextItNet and jointly train a small token-embedding/pooling text branch on permitted titles/descriptions. Add an auxiliary contrastive loss matching each item-ID embedding to its own text representation against other training items; optionally add token reconstruction from item embeddings to encourage concrete lexical distinctions. Remove the auxiliary branch after training, retaining the learned item table and usual NextItNet scorer in one checkpoint per category. Compare against the corrected baseline using fixed macro validation HR@10, monitoring missing-text coverage, auxiliary-loss strength, embedding collapse, and confusion between similarly titled items. Text similarity supplies observable lexical evidence; it does not establish compatibility, ownership requirements, or user intent. Gains from pretrained-text methods should not be assumed to transfer to this scratch-trained auxiliary objective.
